title: Ship the flash-sale release checklist once — a plugin every brand team installs
feature: Plugin engineering: manifest, skills, rules, hooks, MCP and subagents in one bundle; repository vs uploaded vs skills-only installs; revisions; MCP connection after install; proposing edits to shared plugins
prerequisites: Lab 03 done (rules and skills in this repo), so you know what a skill and a rule look like on their own
Repo cloned, `npm install` done at the root (the offline checker and its tests run under `labs/`)
A Devin account where you can open Customize → Plugins; organization-admin rights are needed only for the shared-scope steps
Optional: the Devin CLI installed locally, to load the plugin from a folder on your machine

matrix.integration: Devin web app — Customize → Plugins (Personal scope)
matrix.fixture: Offline: `node labs/04-plugin-engineering/solution/plugin-check.mjs <your-plugin-dir>` reads your folder the way the criteria do
matrix.note: Personal scope needs no admin; install there first, then move to Organization

matrix.integration: Devin web app — Organization scope (org admin)
matrix.fixture: Replay the shared-scope steps with `--revise` and `--propose` in the checker and the injector files
matrix.note: Upload, revision and approval of a proposed edit all happen at this scope

matrix.integration: Second Devin account without plugin edit rights
matrix.note: Needed only to watch a real proposal card arrive for the admin

matrix.fixture: Leave the declared server unconnected, or point a local copy at the `fixtures/mcp` shim (`node fixtures/mcp/shim.mjs --list`)
matrix.note: The plugin declares the server; nobody's credential goes in the bundle

matrix.fixture: Run the hook through `--hook` in the checker
matrix.note: Plugin hooks and plugin subagents load in local sessions only

credentials.fixture_only_story: Without admin rights or any credentials you still build the whole plugin in a folder, check it with the offline checker until it reports no problems, install it at Personal scope from that folder (zip or repository), and replay the shared-scope moments with the injectors: a skills-only brand repo, a partial revision upload, a plugin with inline secrets, and a brand engineer who is not allowed to edit the shared plugin.
not_exercised: Connecting a live PagerDuty account to the plugin's MCP server; the reference answer leaves it declared and unconnected
Approving a proposed edit from a second, non-admin account; the reference answer replays it from the injector fixture

scenarios.clean_state: On `main` with `git status --short` empty, no local `lab04/*` branches, no `~/kade-flash-sale` working folder, and no plugin named `kade-flash-sale` installed at any scope you control (check Customize → Plugins at Personal and Organization). The seed-spec dataset is loaded for both brands.

injectors.name: skills-only-brand-repo
injectors.behaviour: Lumen Home's team says they already have a checklist repo and asks you to install that instead. It has `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and no manifest (`injectors/brand-checklists/`). Predict what name it installs under, what it can and cannot carry, and whether it replaces your plugin.

injectors.name: partial-revision
injectors.behaviour: A brand lead raises the low-stock threshold and uploads a zip containing only the file they changed (`injectors/revision-2/`). Say what the installed plugin contains afterwards, before you look.

injectors.name: inline-secret
injectors.behaviour: A teammate's draft (`injectors/inline-secret/`) pastes a PagerDuty token and an OAuth client secret straight into the manifest, under a display-style name. Find all three problems and say what Devin does with each.

injectors.name: unauthorised-proposer
injectors.behaviour: A Trailhead engineer who cannot edit organization plugins asks their session to change the shared plugin (`injectors/unauthorised-proposer.json`). Show what they get, who has to act, and what the installed plugin contains in the meantime.

injectors.name: hook-fails-open
injectors.behaviour: The security reviewer asks whether the freeze hook is your guarantee that nobody pushes to `main` during a sale. Answer from the documentation, not from your hope.
